summary: A PerformanceTest app that ships with only the generic Microsoft BCPT samples (creating sales orders, purchase orders, posting item journals) measures Business Central's own baseline performance, not the extension it was built to test. Those samples are starting points, not coverage.

title: Commit shared fixture data created inside a lazy Initialize(), or later tests lose it
summary: A test method with no [TransactionModel(...)] attribute defaults to AutoCommit (see transactionmodel-attribute-governs-test-transactions.md): a method that completes without error commits automatically at its own boundary, with no explicit Commit() needed.

title: Cover the full precondition chain in GIVEN, not just the primary record
summary: A [GIVEN] block is only correct if it sets up every precondition the code under test actually reads, not just the record the scenario is "about." For most master-data tests, creating the primary record is enough.

title: Permission tests must actually lower the execution context
summary: TestPermissions describes how a test runner should establish the permission context; the enum value does not itself assign the business permission set being tested. Restrictive is the default and starts from D365 Full Access, requiring the test to lower permissions.

title: RecordRef.Open with Temp = true cannot check the real table
summary: RecordRef.Open(No: Integer [, Temp: Boolean] [, CompanyName: Text]) always takes a real table number. When Temp is true, though, the RecordRef refers to a temporary instance of that table. That instance starts empty and never contains the persisted rows.

title: Reset per-test state before the IsInitialized guard
summary: Standard Business Central test codeunits call a local Initialize procedure at the start of every test method. Global variables in a test codeunit keep their values between the codeunit's test methods, so a Boolean such as IsInitialized lets Initialize run expensive shared setup only once.

title: Exclude a known-valid TableRelation exception via OnAfterRemoveTableRelation
summary: Codeunit 134926 "Table Relation Test" (shipped in BCApps' test app — only consumers that depend on the BC test libraries can subscribe to it) reads Table Relations Metadata tenant-wide across every installed app, not just the current one, and validates each field's type and length against what its…

title: Generate Test Data Programmatically, Never Assume Existing Records
summary: A BC test company normally contains initialized system/setup data — an AL test suite should not assume an empty database, but it must be independent of unrelated business records: create the records and setup it owns rather than looking up a specific code, number, or name assumed to already exist,…

title: Tag test codeunits with FEATURE, SCENARIO, GIVEN, WHEN, and THEN comments
summary: Test codeunits are easier to trust and to review when they carry a four-level comment structure taken from Behaviour-/Acceptance-Test-Driven Development: [FEATURE] once at the top of the codeunit naming the functional area under test, [SCENARIO] above each test procedure stating one falsifiable…

title: Keep exactly one WHEN per test, with narrow exceptions for flow and defect-then-fix tests
summary: This is a testing-design practice, not a BC platform requirement — no AL API enforces it, and it should not gate a change the way a platform-contradicted claim would. Each test procedure should contain exactly one [WHEN] block: one action that triggers the behaviour under test.

title: Configure TestIsolation on the test runner
summary: TestIsolation is a property of a Subtype = TestRunner codeunit, not of the test codeunit being executed. Its default is Disabled. Codeunit rolls back database changes after each test codeunit and Function after each test method, including changes that the code under test explicitly committed.

title: Match TransactionModel to the commit behavior of the code under test
summary: [TransactionModel(...)] declares how a test method interacts with the database's write transaction. The attribute applies only to methods inside a codeunit with SubType = Test and takes one of three values: AutoRollback, AutoCommit, or None.

title: Wire UI handlers and verify meaningful outcomes
summary: A test runs headless, so every UI call on the executed path must be intercepted by a matching handler named in [HandlerFunctions(...)].

title: Separate UI-layer and logic-layer tests into different codeunits
summary: A test codeunit that drives pages through TestPage — opening pages, reading FactBox parts, triggering field OnValidate through the page — is testing a different layer than a codeunit that calls business-logic procedures directly.

title: Use Assert.IsFalse to check a boolean result, not asserterror around Assert.IsTrue
summary: asserterror exists to assert that a statement raises a runtime error; it is not a general-purpose way to invert a boolean check.

title: Generate unique test fixture values with LibraryUtility helpers, not hardcoded literals
summary: A fixture helper that assigns a hardcoded literal to a primary-key field, or to any field the test relies on as a unique lookup identifier, collides the moment two tests, or two runs of the same test, create that fixture without cleanup — and a literal longer than the field allows raises a…

title: Build fixtures with the test Library codeunits, not hand-rolled Init/Insert
summary: BC ships a layer of test Library codeunits — LibrarySales, LibraryPurchase, LibraryERM, LibraryInventory, LibraryRandom and many more — whose job is to create valid records.

title: Verify field editability with TestPage.Editable(), opened in edit mode
summary: Whether a field can actually be changed is a distinct state from whether it is shown or enabled — Editable() and Enabled() are separate TestField functions.

title: Verify field visibility and enabled state with TestPage.Visible()/.Enabled()
summary: A UI test codeunit does not need to inspect table or page properties indirectly to confirm a field is shown or enabled under given conditions.

title: A page field bound to a table field inherits that field's ToolTip
summary: Starting with BC24 (2024 release wave 1), runtime 13.0 supports ToolTip on table fields. A page field bound to a table field inherits the source field's ToolTip when the page control declares none of its own.

title: Sentence-phrase captions use sentence case, not title case
summary: Business Central caption capitalization depends on whether the caption reads as a noun phrase or a sentence/verb phrase.

title: Control add-in accessibility is the developer's responsibility
summary: When a developer builds a JavaScript control add-in, they bypass the Business Central framework's built-in accessibility support and take full responsibility for the accessibility of the rendered HTML, JavaScript, and CSS.

title: Control add-ins cannot use BC color tokens or theming
summary: A JavaScript control add-in has no access to Business Central's color tokens or theming system. The BC client will not push theme variables, accent colors, or high-contrast palettes into the add-in's iframe.

title: Load packaged control add-in resources with credentialed AJAX
summary: JavaScript in a Business Central control add-in can load a static resource from its extension package with AJAX, but the request needs the Business Central context and cookies.

title: Serialize control add-in AL calls and keep payloads small
summary: InvokeExtensibilityMethod crosses from a control add-in into the Business Central service.

title: Cosmetic styles need no textual context
summary: A field's Style property controls text formatting. Some style values are purely cosmetic — they change visual appearance but do not convey semantic meaning. Cosmetic styles never require additional context and must not be reported as accessibility findings:

title: Default descending sort on historical pages
summary: Historical list pages should default to showing the newest records first. On pages such as log entries, ledger entries, archives, and other history lists, an oldest-first default order does not align with the primary use of the page, which is typically to review recent activity.

title: A `DropDown` field remains hidden when its lookup-page control is hidden
summary: A tableextension can append a field to the DropDown field group with addlast, but the client still omits that field when its control on the underlying lookup page has Visible = false. Changing only the table field group therefore compiles while producing no visible UI change.

title: Filter ListPart FactBoxes With SubPageLink To The Parent Record
summary: A FactBox is a page part that surfaces related data beside the main record so users avoid navigating away. Every FactBox runs a database query as its host page loads, so an unfiltered one is a hidden performance tax paid on every page open.

title: Set Field Importance To Drive FastTab Progressive Disclosure
summary: A FastTab field's Importance property controls whether the field is visible immediately, hidden behind "Show more", or surfaced on the collapsed FastTab header summary line.

title: Grid and fixed-layout data-table heuristic
summary: Business Central renders grid() and fixed() layouts in two modes. The mode is chosen automatically by a client heuristic. A grid renders as a data table (HTML <table> with row/column semantics) only when all of the following are true:

title: Group caption quality is not an accessibility issue
summary: Group captions affect page organization, but missing, generic, or duplicate group captions are not accessibility violations per the BC accessibility rules. Do not flag groups for missing, generic, or duplicate captions during an accessibility review.

title: Group-labeled first child exception
summary: ShowCaption = false is acceptable on an editable field only when all of the following conditions are met:

title: Group ShowCaption = false outside grid/fixed is a layout choice
summary: In a standard Card or Document page, a group with ShowCaption = false is a layout choice, not an accessibility violation.

title: Layout-table grids with visible captions are valid
summary: A grid or fixed layout that does not meet all three data-table conditions renders as a layout table. A layout table where editable fields keep their visible captions is not an accessibility violation. Each field is labeled by its own caption — this is a valid, accessible pattern.

title: Open documents from a mixed-type list through Page Management
summary: Some tables back several document pages, chosen by a type field. Sales Header rows open as Sales Quote, Sales Order, Sales Invoice, Sales Credit Memo, Blanket Sales Order, or Sales Return Order, depending on Document Type. A list over such a table cannot use one CardPageID.

title: Nested grids are not supported
summary: A grid nested inside another grid is not a supported pattern in Business Central. Even if an inner grid independently meets the data-table heuristic, the outer grid fails because its groups contain non-field children (the inner grids). The result is broken table semantics for both layers.

title: A notification that must be recalled needs an Id the code can find again
summary: Notification.Recall() withdraws the notification whose Id it carries. When Id is left unassigned, Send() assigns one.

title: OnDrillDown on non-editable fields renders as a link
summary: The Business Central client renders non-editable fields that have an OnDrillDown trigger as HTML <a> (anchor) elements. Screen readers correctly announce these as links. OnDrillDown on a non-editable field is therefore not an accessibility issue — the platform handles the semantics.

title: Offload Slow Read-Only Page Calculations To Background Tasks
summary: Pages that compute statistics, aggregates, or external lookups inline block the page from rendering until the calculation finishes, producing a visible freeze on FactBoxes, cue tiles, and calculated fields.

title: Page client-expression properties must not use an `in [...]` list
summary: Enabled, Visible, Editable, and StyleExpr on page controls (the list is not exhaustive; HideValue is rejected the same way) can be bound to a client expression instead of a literal.

title: Pages must match one of Business Central's page-type conventions
summary: Business Central's page types — RoleCenter, Card, List, CardPart, ListPart, Worksheet, Document, ListPlus, plus system dialog/special types such as NavigatePage, ConfirmationDialog, StandardDialog, HeadlinePart, and API (a selected list of conventional types this article covers design conventions…

title: Promote Actions With The Modern `actionref` Syntax, Never The Legacy `Promoted` Properties
summary: Business Central 2022 release wave 2 (v21) introduced the area(Promoted) block with actionref as the way to promote page actions, separating an action's definition from its promotion. The older approach set Promoted, PromotedCategory, PromotedOnly, and PromotedIsBig directly on each action.

title: Use Standard Promoted Action Group Names And Placements
summary: Business Central ships a fixed vocabulary of promoted action groups, and users build muscle memory around where each kind of action lives.

title: Gate Role Center content by permission with AccessByPermission
summary: A page of type RoleCenter cannot have triggers (AL0378, error) or procedures (AL0569, warning that will become an error), and the AL compiler applies both rules to a pageextension whose target is a Role Center.

title: Semantic styles in a cuegroup are auto-labeled
summary: Fields inside a cuegroup render as cue tiles. The Business Central client automatically provides an accessible label for semantic styles on cue tiles (for example, "Favorable", "Unfavorable").

title: Semantic styles need independent textual meaning
summary: Three Style values carry semantic meaning through color and must be backed by text that conveys the same meaning:

title: Preserve list scope after `SetSelectionFilter`
summary: CurrPage.SetSelectionFilter(Rec) behaves differently depending on whether the user explicitly multi-selected rows. When no rows are marked — the cursor is simply positioned on a row — the method writes a primary key filter for that single row and leaves MarkedOnly as false.

title: ShowCaption = false on non-editable fields
summary: When a field is explicitly non-editable (Editable = false), it serves as content rather than as a form field. In that case, ShowCaption = false is acceptable: there is no input control whose label could be lost.

title: ShowCaption in a PromptDialog prompt area
summary: On PageType = PromptDialog pages, input fields inside area(Prompt) are labeled by the dialog's heading — the page Caption. Setting ShowCaption = false on such an input field is the standard pattern and should not be flagged, provided the page has a Caption.

title: ShowCaption inside a repeater is harmless
summary: Fields inside a repeater() control are labeled by their column headers, not by their own captions. ShowCaption = false on a field inside a repeater is harmless and should not be flagged.

title: ShowCaption on editable fields
summary: ShowCaption must remain true (the default) on editable fields unless the field matches one of the officially supported "magic patterns". Fields are editable by default.

title: Mark code-required page fields with ShowMandatory
summary: ShowMandatory draws the red asterisk on a page field and, per the platform documentation, enforces no validation.

title: Standalone content in a layout-table grid
summary: A non-editable field with ShowCaption = false is acceptable inside a layout-table grid only when the field is standalone content — it displays a value that is meaningful on its own (for example a status message or a description) and is not intended to label or be labeled by another field in the…

title: StyleExpr: Boolean toggle vs Text variable
summary: StyleExpr on a page field serves two distinct purposes depending on its type:

title: Tabular intent requires data-table conditions
summary: The most common accessibility bug in grid layouts is partially following the data-table conventions. A developer arranges fields with tabular intent — one field acts as a label or row header for another — but the grid does not satisfy all the data-table heuristic conditions.

title: Use `UpdatePropagation = Both` when line edits must refresh the main page
summary: A page part does not automatically refresh its parent page when the subpage changes. UpdatePropagation = Subpage updates only the part; Both also refreshes the main page.

title: Validate request-page input in OnQueryClosePage, not only in OnPreReport
summary: OnPreReport runs after the request page has closed and before the data items are processed. A validation error raised there aborts the run with the request page already gone: everything the user typed is lost, and the only way forward is to open the report again and retype it.

title: `ModuleInfo.AppVersion` changes meaning with execution context
summary: ModuleInfo.AppVersion() is the installed version during normal operation, the version being installed inside install code, and the target version inside upgrade code. It is therefore not the source data version during an upgrade.

title: Primary-key and field-type changes are safe only on tables without existing data
summary: Primary-key changes and field-type changes (for example widening Integer to BigInteger) rewrite the on-disk layout of every row in the table. On a new feature table that ships in the same change as the modification, no rows exist and the change is free.

title: Upgrade check triggers do not migrate data
summary: OnCheckPreconditionsPerCompany/PerDatabase run before the upgrade to verify that it can start. OnValidateUpgradePerCompany/PerDatabase run after upgrade logic to verify that it succeeded. Treat both phases as read-only checks.

title: Use `DataTransfer` for bulk updates on large tables
summary: Tables that can contain more than 300,000 records, and any newly added field on an existing table, should be initialized with DataTransfer rather than a repeat ... Modify ... until Next() = 0 loop.

title: `DataTransfer` does not fire validation triggers or event subscribers
summary: DataTransfer writes sets directly at the database layer, so row-based triggers and events do not run. For CopyFields, that includes the table OnModify trigger and OnBeforeModifyEvent/OnAfterModifyEvent; direct field assignment also does not call field OnValidate or its validation events.

title: Log telemetry; do not raise errors that block the upgrade
summary: When upgrade code encounters unexpected data — a record it expected to find, a relationship it assumed to be intact — the response is to log telemetry and continue, not to raise an error.

title: Add new enum values only at the end
summary: An AL enum is a fixed list of ordinal-named values. Persisted rows reference enum members by ordinal, not by name. The only enum mutation that preserves the meaning of every existing row is appending a new value at the end — every previously valid ordinal still maps to the same member.

title: Detect first install with `DataVersion() = Version.Create('0.0.0.0')`
summary: On the first install of an extension on a tenant the platform records a zero data version: AppInfo.DataVersion() returns Version.Create('0.0.0.0'). During reinstall, DataVersion() identifies the previously installed data version.

title: Guard every database read in upgrade code with `if`
summary: Inside an upgrade codeunit (or any procedure transitively invoked from OnUpgradePerCompany / OnUpgradePerDatabase), an unguarded Record.Get, Record.FindSet, or Record.FindLast raises a runtime error when the row or set is missing.

title: Hybrid migration codeunits are not standard upgrade codeunits
summary: Codeunits like HybridBC14, HybridSL, HybridGP, and HybridBaseDeployment implement one-time migration paths from a specific source system into Business Central.

title: `InitValue` does not back-fill existing rows
summary: InitValue on a field defines the value the platform assigns when a *new* record is inserted. It does not touch rows that already exist when the field is added.

title: Separate install or upgrade codeunits have no execution order
summary: An extension can contain multiple Install or Upgrade codeunits, but Business Central does not guarantee the order in which codeunits of the same subtype execute.

title: Install code does not run during a version upgrade
summary: An install codeunit runs when an extension is installed for the first time or an uninstalled version is installed again. Installing a higher extension version through the data-upgrade operation does not invoke OnInstallAppPerCompany or OnInstallAppPerDatabase.

title: Keep upgrade validation checks bounded
summary: Triggers such as OnValidateUpgradePerCompany run on every upgrade pass. A full-table scan or cross-table validation therefore adds cost to every upgrade of every tenant. Validation is a read-only lifecycle check, so it cannot make itself one-time by writing an upgrade tag.

title: Upgrade code must not use ChangeCompany
summary: The platform upgrades each company in its own context: OnUpgradePerCompany (like the other PerCompany upgrade and install triggers) runs once per company, in a separate system session opened for that company, while PerDatabase triggers run in a session that opens no company.

title: No external calls inside upgrade codeunits
summary: Upgrade code runs in a constrained execution window: the tenant is mid-upgrade, no users are signed in, and a failure aborts the entire transaction.

title: Stage obsoletion `Pending → Removed`; write upgrade code on removal
summary: ObsoleteState has a deliberate two-step lifecycle. Pending keeps the element compilable and present — callers still find it but receive a deprecation warning.

title: ObsoleteReason need not restate the removal version; ObsoleteTag carries it
summary: An obsoleted object, field, key, enum, or enum value carries both ObsoleteReason and ObsoleteTag, and the two properties have different jobs. ObsoleteReason is free text that explains why the element is obsolete and what replaces it.

title: Give every obsolete element a reason and tag
summary: AL has two obsoletion mechanisms, depending on the symbol:

title: Register upgrade tags that must be seeded for new companies
summary: SetUpgradeTag(Tag) directly records a completed per-company upgrade step; HasUpgradeTag(Tag) can then guard that step on later upgrades.

title: Skip non-essential runtime work when `GetExecutionContext() = ExecutionContext::Upgrade`
summary: Runtime procedures (table triggers, install routines, helpers called from many places) sometimes fire during the upgrade window because the upgrade itself touches the data they react to.

title: `OnUpgradePerCompany` / `OnUpgradePerDatabase` should call helpers, not inline logic
summary: The OnUpgradePerCompany and OnUpgradePerDatabase triggers on an upgrade codeunit are dispatch points, not implementation slots. They should contain only calls to named local procedures — one call per feature being upgraded.

title: Unreleased schema changes need no upgrade or migration path
summary: Upgrade and migration findings protect data and schema that have already shipped to customers.

title: Upgrade logic must live in a codeunit with `Subtype = Upgrade`
summary: A codeunit only participates in the upgrade pipeline when it sets Subtype = Upgrade. The platform then permits and dispatches the OnUpgradePerCompany and OnUpgradePerDatabase triggers on that codeunit during upgrade.

title: Never nest upgrade tag checks or blend two migrations under one tag
summary: Upgrade tag *checks* should stay flat: never nest one tag's existence check inside another tag's guarded body, and never let one tagged procedure quietly perform a second, functionally distinct migration — that turns two upgrade steps into one that can't be tracked, skipped, or fixed…

title: Control upgrade execution with upgrade tags, not version checks
summary: Each piece of upgrade logic must run exactly once per company (or database) across the lifetime of an extension. The platform mechanism for that is the Upgrade Tag codeunit: a procedure asks HasUpgradeTag(MyTag()) at entry, performs its work, then calls SetUpgradeTag(MyTag()) to record completion.

title: Under OData schema version 2.0 an API enum field is a contract by member name; under 1.0 it is the caption
summary: What an API page publishes for an enum field depends on the OData $schemaversion the caller receives, and never on the ordinal.

title: Keep Consumer-Provided Key Fields Editable on API Pages
summary: A field listed in ODataKeyFields cannot have Editable = false when the API page allows inserts and the field's value must be supplied by the caller. Marking it read-only removes the field from the OData write schema, so a POST that includes it is rejected as an unknown property.

title: Give API pages least-privilege write access
summary: A general-purpose API page that exposes many fields should not be widened to allow writes on one additional field.

title: Check HTTP status before consuming the response body
summary: A successful AL HttpClient call only confirms that the platform completed the HTTP exchange. The server can still return 4xx or 5xx, often with an error document whose shape differs from the expected success payload.

title: Check for JSON null before converting a value
summary: An optional property in a JSON payload can be missing or present with the value null, and the two cases behave differently in AL. When the Boolean result is captured, JsonObject.Get returns false for a missing key but true for "email": null, because the key exists.

title: Lock down write operations on read-only API pages
summary: An API meant purely for reading — a reporting or lookup endpoint — is not read-only just because nobody intends to write to it.

title: Read only committed data from APIs that must not expose in-flight writes
summary: This is about the data-consistency contract of an API endpoint: what a consumer receives when it reads. By default an API read can return in-flight rows that a concurrent, still-open transaction has written but not yet committed.

title: Expose business operations as bound actions, not as writable status flags
summary: An API consumer that needs to *do* something to a record — post it, ship it, release it — should call an explicit operation, not mutate a field and hope a side effect fires.

title: Address API records by SystemId, not by a renamable business key
summary: Every BC table carries a SystemId — an immutable GUID assigned at insert and never reused. API consumers must address a record through a key that does not change, otherwise a previously stored URL or @odata.id reference breaks the moment a user renames the underlying business key.

title: Format exchanged values with standard format 9
summary: Format(Value) uses standard format 0, the display format, and follows the current user's regional settings. The same decimal renders as -76.543,21 for a European region and -76,543.21 for English (US); the same date renders as 05-04-21 or 04/05/21.

title: Handle HttpClient platform failure before accessing the response
summary: AL HttpClient methods can fail before a usable HTTP response exists because of an invalid request, DNS or network failure, certificate validation, timeout, a disabled extension setting, or the response-size limit.

title: Link API parts on SystemId and choose the correct multiplicity
summary: Multiplicity is available from runtime 6.3 (Business Central 17.3) and defaults an API page part to a 1:N collection. The multiplicity-specific guidance therefore does not apply to BC 17.0 through 17.2.

title: Declare API routing properties and an explicit stable version
summary: An API page needs APIPublisher, APIGroup, EntityName, EntitySetName, and a backing SourceTable to define its routed entity. APIVersion is different: it is optional at the language level and defaults to beta.

title: Set the text encoding when converting exchanged text to or from BLOB bytes
summary: Blob.CreateInStream and Blob.CreateOutStream take an optional TextEncoding; when it is omitted, the stream uses MSDos (OEM) encoding, whose code page depends on the server's system locale. Encoding matters when an operation converts between AL text and bytes, such as WriteText or ReadText.

title: Recalculate Stored Derived Fields Before Exposing Them on API Pages
summary: A stored field whose value is derived from other fields inside an OnValidate trigger only updates when that specific trigger fires. If the underlying source data changes through some other path, the stored value goes stale without raising any error.

title: Version changed API shapes with a new page object
summary: Once an API version is published, external clients depend on its exact shape — entity names, fields, keys, and behavior — as a stable contract. APIVersion can list several versions on one API page, but every listed route is generated from that same page object and therefore exposes the same shape.

title: Verify webhook eligibility and complete every validationToken handshake
summary: Business Central can subscribe only to eligible API pages, not every endpoint that can be read through an API.

title: France (FR)
summary: France localization of Business Central 29. It covers payment management with payment slips, RIB bank keys, SIREN/SIRET company data, fiscal period and year closing, FEC and XML audit exports, accelerated (derogatory) depreciation, VAT paid on debits, Intrastat/DEB and service declarations. It answers where French-specific behavior sits in code and on Learn.

title: UnitedKingdom (GB)
summary: United Kingdom (GB) localization of Business Central 29. It covers Making Tax Digital VAT returns to HMRC, GovTalk and EC Sales List submission, reverse charge VAT, UK postcode address lookup, VAT audit and GB document reports, BACS and check printing, and UK fixed asset depreciation.

title: India (IN)
summary: India localization for Business Central 29 adds GST (including cess, reverse charge, advance payments, input service distribution, reconciliation, settlement), TDS and TCS, e-invoice and e-way bill, voucher interface, gate entry, subcontracting, FA depreciation and stale cheques. Use it for questions on Indian tax setup, posting and local reports.

title: Iceland (IS)
summary: Iceland (IS) localization of Business Central 29, delivered as the IS Core app on top of W1. It covers IRS number mapping to the chart of accounts, tax authority reports, VAT summary on documents, electronic invoicing for single-copy invoices, registration numbers, and deletion of posted invoices and credit memos.

title: Italy (IT)
summary: Italy (IT) localization of Business Central 29. It covers Italian VAT (settlement, registers, VAT transactions reports, nondeductible VAT), withholding tax and INPS contributions, customer and vendor bills, FatturaPA e-invoicing, Intrastat, fiscal inventory valuation, Italian fixed asset depreciation and legacy subcontracting.

title: Mexico (MX)
summary: Mexico (MX) localization of Business Central 29. It covers CFDI 4.0 electronic invoicing with PAC stamping and SAT certificates, Carta de Porte for transfers and shipments, DIOT reports, electronic accounting export, cash-basis VAT, tax identification (RFC, CURP) and electronic bank payments. It also carries NA-derived sales tax, bank reconciliation and report objects.

title: Netherlands (NL)
summary: Netherlands (NL) localization of Business Central 29. It covers Dutch telebanking (payment proposals, payment history, SEPA ISO 20022 export, bank statement import), cash and bank/giro journals, electronic VAT and ICP declarations via Digipoort, CMR notes, the tax authority audit file, Dutch post codes and Intrastat.

title: Norway (NO)
summary: Norway localization of Business Central 29. It covers Norwegian VAT codes and proportional VAT, SAF-T export, electronic VAT returns, remittance and OCR/KID banking, EHF and PEPPOL e-invoicing, recurring sales orders and payroll import. Use it for questions about local fields, setup and reports.

title: NewZealand (NZ)
summary: New Zealand localization of Business Central 29. It adds GST (with prepayment and full-GST handling), withholding tax (WHT), BAS and IRD number fields, tax invoices and adjustment notes, EFT vendor payments, post-dated checks, cost-plus pricing and local reports. Use it for questions on NZ tax, banking and address functionality.

title: Russia (RU)
summary: Russia localization of Business Central 29. It adds Russian accounting and tax functionality: VAT ledgers and settlement, G/L correspondence, prepayment differences, fixed assets, cash and bank orders, tax registers, and statutory print forms (TORG, M-, FA-, CO- series). It answers what Russia-specific setup, posting and reports exist.

title: Sweden (SE)
summary: Sweden (SE) localization of Business Central 29. It covers SIE import and export of general ledger data, automatic account codes, EU third-party purchase reporting, Swedish balance sheet and income statement reports, PEPPOL 3.0 for Sweden, and Swedish extensions of document reports. It answers what Sweden adds to W1 and where Learn documents it.

title: UnitedStates (US)
summary: United States (US) localization of Business Central 29. It covers sales and use tax (tax areas, jurisdictions, external tax engine), IRS 1099 and 1096 reporting with IRIS, EFT and ACH payments, checks, bank reconciliation and deposits. It also carries North American reports and Mexican CFDI and Canadian tax pieces.
